scope: All three lenses (spec-compliance, security, architecture) over plan.md, research.md and tasks.md, judged against spec.md, decisions.md, planning-notes.md, sketch.md, CONSTITUTION.md, CONTEXT.md, the Django and testing standards and ADRs 0010-0012. The schema allows one top-level lens, so each finding's claim opens with its own lens tag. Code read: mvp_payments/stripe/{views,models,client,apps,checks,urls}.py, mvp_payments/{views,urls,plans_urls}.py, namespaces/{stripe,stripe_plans}.py, templatetags/mvp_payments.py, cotton/stripe/plan*.html and mvp_payments/stripe/plans.html, tests/stripe_fake.py, tests/test_app.py, tests/test_contributions.py, tests/test_views.py. I ran pytest on test_urls, test_app, test_contributions and test_views: 23 failed, 69 passed on the branch as it stands. Coverage checks: FR against tasks 22 of 22, each with a task and a planned test; SC against tasks 8 of 8; edge cases 9 of 9, one with no task (DMP-001). Routes and their rules, 4 of 4 plus the tag: payments_plans:stripe-plans is public (ADR 0012); payments:stripe-checkout is LoginRequired, POST only, CSRF through the project's middleware, takes only a price in the catalogue, and checks return_to; payments:stripe-billing-return is LoginRequired, and its session_id is untrusted but goes through the signed reference; payments:stripe-webhook verifies the signature first; {% stripe_plans %} has no route and reads the request. New code against the tree: 9 of 9 checked (Catalogue, StripeConfig.catalogue, Customer.start_checkout, CheckoutView, the webhook branch, plans_urls, PlanChoices, the three filters, the tag). research.md lists 2 of them, and the only overlap with existing code is DMP-009. I checked both sides of each rule I relied on: Catalogue.price() returns None both when the price is absent and when there is no catalogue at all (DMP-011); from_checkout's existing-customer branch (DMP-001); clear() seen from another process (DMP-002). SDK claims checked in stripe 16 site-packages: auto_paging_iter carries the original filters (and the expand) to the next page (stripe/_list_object.py:119-140, 195-203, 223-224); to_dict recurses by default (stripe/_stripe_object.py:562-598); PriceListParams takes active, expand, limit and type (stripe/params/_price_list_params.py:9-54); the Checkout Session create params take allow_promotion_codes, cancel_url, client_reference_id, customer, customer_email, mode and success_url (stripe/params/checkout/_session_create_params.py:19,107,111,133,163,284,402); the HTTP client's default timeout is 80 s (stripe/_http_client.py:512).

findings.claim: [spec-compliance] The spec's edge case 'a signed-in person whose Stripe customer Stripe no longer has: checkout is created without it' has no task and no test, and with the planned flow that person can never buy.
findings.evidence: spec.md Edge Cases, 6th bullet. tasks.md T005 lists no missing-customer case. plan.md §Stripe app models.py passes the user's existing customer. mvp_payments/stripe/models.py:76-78: Customer.for_user returns the stale row. Stripe then refuses the session with resource_missing, and CheckoutView turns that into 'could not be started' on every attempt (plan.md views.py bullet). If a session is ever created without the customer, models.py:139-150 (from_checkout) logs an error and returns None, because the user already has a Customer with a different stripe_id. Neither the return view nor the webhook then ties the purchase. Only models.py:257-262 (sync on a resource_missing customer) deletes the stale row, and the planned CheckoutView never calls it.
findings.reproduction: A user has a Customer row cus_old. cus_old is deleted in Stripe and the customer.deleted webhook is missed. The user presses Choose: the session create gets 400 resource_missing, an error message is shown, and the same happens every time after.
findings.suggested_fix: T005: when start_checkout gets InvalidRequestError with code resource_missing on the customer, call customer.sync(), which deletes the stale row (models.py:257-262), and create the session again without a customer. Add one FakeStripe test for this. T006: tie with from_checkout() whenever Customer.for_user() is None at return time, so the purchase is tied once the stale row is gone.

findings.claim: [architecture] Clearing the catalogue on a webhook or from stripe_sync only works when the project's default cache is shared between processes. Django's default is per-process, and nothing in the plan says so. T008's in-process tests pass whatever the cache backend.
findings.evidence: .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/conf/global_settings.py:522-526: the default CACHES is LocMemCache, which is per-process. plan.md §Stripe app, catalogue.py, uses Django's default cache. stripe_sync is a management command, a separate process, so its clear() empties its own empty LocMem instance and nothing else (FR-015 sync clause, US3 scenario 6). A webhook clears only the worker that received it, so other workers show the old catalogue until the expiry (SC-004 'the next time it is shown after the verified webhook'). research.md 'Demo cache' already chooses a file-based cache so the seed and the server share it, so the plan knows about the requirement. It just isn't documented for consumers.
findings.reproduction: A project with no CACHES setting runs gunicorn with 4 workers. A price is renamed in Stripe and the verified price.updated webhook lands on worker 1. Workers 2-4 serve the old name for up to an hour, and `manage.py stripe_sync` changes nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: T008: state in docs/reference/plans-page.md and docs/how-to/install-the-stripe-app.md that webhook and sync clearing reach the page only when the default cache is shared across processes (not LocMemCache or DummyCache), and that with any other backend changes arrive when the catalogue expires. No code change.

findings.claim: [security] The public plans page caches nothing when Stripe fails, so during a Stripe outage every anonymous page view makes a blocking Stripe request with the SDK's 80-second default timeout.
findings.evidence: plan.md §Stripe app: 'A missing secret key or a Stripe error is logged by error type and returns None, caching nothing'. tasks.md T001 tests exactly that. mvp_payments/stripe/client.py:34-36 builds the client with the SDK's default HTTP client, whose timeout is 80 s (.venv/.../stripe/_http_client.py:512). The page is unauthenticated (FR-006, ADR 0012), and {% stripe_plans %} on a landing page has the same exposure.
findings.reproduction: api.stripe.com stops answering (a blackholed connection, not a refusal). Each anonymous GET of /plans/ or the landing page holds a worker for up to 80 s. A few dozen visitors, or a script, use up the worker pool and take down the whole site, not only the plans.
findings.suggested_fix: Catalogue.prices(): on a Stripe error, cache the unavailable result under the same key for a short fixed period (say 60 s; clear() still removes it). Change T001's 'cache nothing' assertion to 'a failure is not fetched again within that period, and a later call after it fetches'. A missing secret key makes no request, so it needs no change. FR-016 still holds: a catalogue already cached is never overwritten, because this only happens on a miss.

findings.claim: [spec-compliance] 23 existing tests fail on the branch because the sketch moved the plans page. The tasks name only some of them, and several are guards for Articles XIII and XIV. Rewriting them without a record will hit S6's 'pre-existing test edited' blocking check, or they will be deleted without anyone deciding to.
findings.evidence: pytest tests/test_urls.py tests/test_app.py tests/test_contributions.py tests/test_views.py: 23 failed. Outside TestPlansPage, which T004's 'and their tests' covers, the failures are: test_urls.py::TestPaymentURLs::test_declared_page_name_reverses_to_its_view[stripe-plans-PlansPageView] and ::test_a_page_kept_out_of_the_navigation_still_reverses; test_contributions.py::TestPage::test_the_stripe_namespace_opens_only_its_plans_page_to_everyone and ::TestNamespaceIndependence::test_neither_namespaces_pages_resolve_to_the_others; test_views.py::TestPaymentPage::test_a_page_may_be_declared_open_to_everyone, which guards Page.login_required (contributions.py:50), now with no user in the package; TestSubscriptionPage (2, from views.py:125 reverse('stripe-plans'), which T003 fixes); TestPlansPageOverride::test_a_projects_own_page_template_receives_every_documented_context_name. test_app.py:55 and test_contributions.py:298,335 still reverse 'payments:stripe-plans'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to T003 a list of each of these tests and what happens to it: rewritten against payments_plans:stripe-plans, or retired with the reason the guarded behaviour no longer exists. For Page.login_required, either keep the option with its test rebuilt on a test-only page, or record its removal. That choice is the maintainer's, so the plan should name it rather than leave it to the Implementer.

findings.claim: [spec-compliance] If the success address is built by passing the whole '...?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}' string through request.build_absolute_uri(), as research.md describes, the braces are percent-encoded. Stripe then does not substitute the session id, and FR-011's first-purchase tie on return fails.
findings.evidence: research.md 'Absolute URLs for Stripe. request.build_absolute_uri() on the reversed paths', together with 'the existing return view with ?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}'. .venv/.../django/http/request.py:300 returns iri_to_uri(location), and django/utils/encoding.py:135 quotes with safe='/#%[]=:;$&()+,!?*@'~', which does not include { or }. Likely, not verified, because I cannot check offline whether Stripe accepts %7BCHECKOUT_SESSION_ID%7D.
findings.suggested_fix: plan.md views.py bullet: build the absolute URL of the reversed return path first and append '?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}' after it. In T005, assert that the success_url posted to FakeStripe contains the literal '{CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}'.

findings.claim: [architecture] The plan's constitution check says Article XI is met, but the interface's view and template tag now cause a Stripe request on every cache miss, and the provider app keeps a copy of the catalogue. Both contradict Article XI as written, and the plan only amends its sentence about where a plan is chosen. That is a constitution change the PR has to put to Sam explicitly.
findings.evidence: CONSTITUTION.md Article XI says the interface 'holds no state and talks to no provider', a view 'may not ... reach a provider', and a provider app keeps 'the smallest local copy ... who the provider's customer is, and that customer's subscription'. It also says plans are chosen in 'the provider's checkout, pricing table and portal' and that the app 'never builds a checkout, plan-change or cancellation screen of its own'. plan.md Constitution check row XI amends only the plan-choice wording. Reaching the catalogue through apps.get_app_config() (plan.md §Interface) gets past tests/test_app.py:93-122, which bans only imports, but it does not meet the rule's text.
findings.suggested_fix: plan.md §Documentation, the convergence list: name the Article XI bullets that change. (a) An interface view or tag may ask a provider app for its cached catalogue, which the app reads from the provider on a miss. (b) A provider app may also keep the provider's catalogue in the project's cache, never in the database. (c) Plans are chosen on a page drawn by the package and paid for on the provider's checkout. Flag these in the PR body as constitution amendments for the maintainer.

findings.claim: [spec-compliance] CheckoutView cannot distinguish 'Stripe unavailable' from 'price not on offer'. Catalogue.price() returns None for both, so during an outage on a cold cache the person is told the plan is no longer on offer, where FR-018 says they should be told the checkout could not be started.
findings.evidence: plan.md §Stripe app: price(price_id) -> dict | None, and prices() returns None on failure. The views.py bullet says 'price not in the catalogue → warning message'. A cold cache at POST time is reachable: the catalogue expires between page load and click, or under LocMem the POST reaches another worker (DMP-002).
findings.suggested_fix: T005: check `Catalogue.prices() is None` first, which gives the error message and a return (FR-018). Only after that treat a missing price as 'no longer on offer'. Add one test with the catalogue unavailable.

findings.claim: [architecture] T001's 'every page fetched' test cannot be written with FakeStripe as it is, contrary to research.md's 'already answers list endpoints'. With has_more true it would loop forever.
findings.evidence: tests/stripe_fake.py:49-60: respond_with_list always sets has_more False. :35 and :150 key routes by (method, path) only, ignoring the query, so the SDK's second-page request with starting_after (stripe/_list_object.py:195-203) gets the same canned page again. With has_more true, auto_paging_iter never stops. Spec edge case 'more prices than Stripe returns in one response'.
findings.suggested_fix: T001: add a paged list response to FakeStripe, with consecutive pages for one path and has_more true on all but the last, and name it in the task.

findings.claim: [architecture] T007 plans a test that the picked price is 'outlined'. That is a styling assertion, which the testing standard forbids. Drop it, which removes work.
findings.evidence: tasks.md T007 'the picked price outlined and its frequency selected'. The outline is cotton/stripe/plan_card.html:9 (border-primary versus border-base-100). docs/contributing/standards/testing.md §1 'Not tested: Styling and layout: colours ...'. Article XV forbids assertions on a class name.
findings.suggested_fix: T007: keep 'its frequency selected' (the checked radio, plans.html:17, and x-data first_interval) and the card's id anchor. Remove 'the picked price outlined'.

findings.claim: [architecture] Two places build a throwaway CurrentSubscription with five blank fields only to borrow frequency_display. That is a copy that will drift.
findings.evidence: mvp_payments/namespaces/stripe_plans.py:44-52 (PlanChoices.interval_label) and mvp_payments/templatetags/mvp_payments.py:84-92 (price_frequency) each construct CurrentSubscription(status='', name='', amount=None, ..., period_start=None, period_end=None). T002 keeps both.
findings.suggested_fix: T002: give the frequency wording an entry on CurrentSubscription that takes (interval, interval_count), such as a staticmethod that frequency_display calls, and use it from both places.

findings.claim: [architecture] {% stripe_plans %} in a project template raises LookupError when mvp_payments.stripe is not installed, because the tag is registered whenever the interface is. A landing page then 500s, against Article XIII's 'a page that cannot resolve is not a broken page'.
findings.evidence: plan.md §Interface: PlanChoices reads apps.get_app_config('mvp_payments_stripe'), which raises LookupError for an app that is not installed. templatetags/mvp_payments.py:60-65 is registered by the interface app, and demo/templates/demo/home.html:71 uses it. T003 covers 'not routed without the Stripe app' for the page only.
findings.suggested_fix: T009: when apps.is_installed('mvp_payments.stripe') is false, PlanChoices.for_request returns prices None, so the parts render nothing. Add one test under settings_without_stripe_app.

notes: research.md 'What already exists' lists 2 new pieces (catalogue, tag). It leaves out PlanChoices, CheckoutView, Customer.start_checkout, plans_urls, StripeConfig.catalogue, the three filters and the webhook branch. None of these duplicates existing code beyond DMP-009.
plan.md 'Stories and order' says 'Sequential, one implementer at a time' and also 'US2–US4 together'. Pick one wording.

Pricing-table references the plan does not name. demo/templates/base.html:10 and :14 load js.stripe.com pricing-table.js and pricing_table.js on every demo page, /plans/ included, which conflicts with US1 scenario 7 on the demo. Also docs/reference/user-subscriptions-page.md:223, cotton/stripe/plans_link.html:6 (comment, also stale against ADR 0012), AGENTS.md:56-57, README.md:36, 118, 167, 215, ADR 0011:11-23, ADR 0008, demo/.env.example, models.py:244 (sync docstring), stripe/views.py:160 (PlanSwitchView docstring), tests/project_app/templates/cotton/stripe/pricing_table.html and tests/project_app/templates/mvp_payments/stripe/plans.html.
CONSTITUTION.md Article XII's paragraph on <stripe-pricing-table>, and Article XIV's example <c-stripe.plan-grid>, should read as current state once the pricing table is gone.
CONTEXT.md 'Plans page' (through Stripe's own pricing table) and 'Checkout' (a component starts it) need current-state wording. The plan names the first only.

BillingReturnView: from_checkout ties a customer to the user in the signed reference, not to request.user. The plan should say the view syncs only a customer whose user is the requester. There is no exposure either way, because only correct rows are written.
Ordering 'products by cheapest price' compares minor units across currencies in a mixed-currency catalogue. Harmless, but worth one line in the reference.
plans.html:37 gives the checkout note a fixed id. Two placements on one page duplicate it, and aria-describedby becomes ambiguous.

{% stripe_plans %} reads context['request'], so it needs the request context processor. Document that. A placement made with the tag gets no unavailable or empty state, which only the page template draws.

The spec edge case 'price archived between load and pick': if the project has not added the price events to its webhook, the archived price stays in the cache, Stripe refuses the session, and the person sees 'could not be started' rather than 'no longer on offer'. Acceptable once documented.
